0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 4 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 17 December 1984, after the draft finalized by the Pig Iron and Cast Iron Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council.
0.2 This standard was first published in 1964. While reviewing this standard the committee took note of the fact that during recent years production of ingot steels has gone up many folds and various sizes of felt that this standard ingot moulds are being used, the Committee should be split up into the following parts: a) Part 1 Bottom stools for large tonne and higher, b) Part 2 Grey cast tonnes, iron ingot size ingot of moulds mass weighing more than one one and eight eight tonne tonne shall

of mass more than up to parts

d) Part 4 Grey cast iron in-got moulds of mass i) Without hot tops, and 11) With hot tops. 0.2.1 This standard is one of the series of the above be covering ingot mould of mass up to one tonne.

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard. is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 3

11.2 The casting shall conform to dimensions of the drawing. If manufacturer apprehends any genuine dificulty, it shall be sorted out with the purchaser before undertaking the actual manufacture. 12. PREPARATION OF MOULDS

12.1 Ingot moulds should be cast in sand moulds. The sand mould should have green hardness 80-90 and bottom hardness 88 min. Dry strength of the mixture should be more than O-6 MPa and permeability more than 150. Moulds should be provided with sufficient vents and should be adequately dried. 13. FREEDOM FROM DEFECTS the cast iron ipearlitic-ferritic 13.1 It is desirable to have structure of without the presence of free cementite.

13.2 Inside surface of ingot mould should be clean and free from defects like seams, sand depression, projects, cracks, crust, cavities, cold shut, scabs, etc. 14. RECTIFICATION 14.1 No weld rectification of inside grinding to smoothen the surface. 15. DEFECTS ON OUTSIDE surface shall be permitted before

SURFACE

15.1 Outside surface also should be defect free. However, if defects do occur, purchaser and manufacturer may decide mutually whether to accept it without rectification, allow rectification or reject it. 16. MACHINING OF TOP/BOTTOM FACE

16.1 Machining of bottom face is not required but bottom face should be reasonably flat and perpendicular to the mould axis in the as cast condition. ( Maximum permissible undulation; f 2 mm. ) 16.2 Top face of the moulds purchaser. shall be machined if required by the

16.3 In pencil ingot moulds, bottom face shall always be machined and shall be perpendicular to vertical axis of mould. Top face need not be machined. 17. PERMISSIBLE DEVIATION

17.1 Permissible deviation in the ingot mould dimensions from the drawing dimensions shall be generally as specified in Table 2. Deviation more than specified may be accommodated by mutual agreement between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 6

FOR USING

18.1 Guidelines for using the ingot moulds for are given in Appendix A for information only. 19. SAMPLING FOR CHEMICAL

ANALYSIS

19.1 Two spoon samples shall be taken during the pouring of each cast or ladle when about one-third and two-thirds of the metal has been
spoon samples so obtained shall be cast separately in form of 30 mm diameter bars about 75 mm long. Alternatively, the mould may be filled directly from the metal stream. The test bars shall be suitably marked so that the castings they represent could be identified.
dry sand in the

discharged.

The

19.2 After cleaning the surface, two flats shall be gound near the bottom of each test bar and the test bar drilled with a 25 mm drill from one clean surface to the other. The speed of the drill should not be more than 9 to 10 rev/min. Drilling after being thoroughly mixed shall constitute the sample for chemical analysis.

19.3 For the determination

of total carbon, the liquid metal shall be poured into a special split mould ( see Fig. 1 ). This gives pins of iron 3 mm in diameter which can be broken off and used directly for carbon determination. RE-TEST AND REJECTION

20.

20.1 If a sample selected for testing fails to meet the requirements specified under 5.1, the purchaser shall select two further samples from the same cast or ladle. If on testing, either of these samples fails to meet the specified requirements, the whole lot shall be deemed as not ,complying with this standard. 7

21.2 The material may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
